scripts._comment_mobile: The trailing `--` is load-bearing. Without it, `npm run mobile -- --port 8082` is parsed by npm itself: npm eats `--port`, passes a bare `8082` on to `expo start`, and expo reads it as a project root and dies with 'Invalid project root'. With it, the arguments reach expo. APP_TARGET works the same way: `APP_TARGET=japa npm run mobile -- --port 8082` (set it in the shell, not after `--`, because it is read by app.config.ts and not by expo's CLI).
scripts._comment_theme_audit: The item-19 dark-mode test, applied to every screen file at once: each route is opened in both colorSchemes and the screen's own colours must move. Writes PNGs to %TEMP%/theme-audit and exits 1 on a screen that did not.
scripts._comment_check_game: The two gates above are about the store listing. This one is about the game: it loads apps/mobile/lib/block-clear.ts in plain Node and asserts the rules, so it runs anywhere — the screenshot probes need Playwright and a preview, and those only exist on the capture VM.
scripts._comment_check_merge: The second game engine, same shape: apps/mobile/lib/merge-tiles.ts is loaded in plain Node and the merge rule is asserted on hand-written lines. `check:games` is what a change to either engine should run — a tile game whose 2,2,4 slides to 8 scores the same as one that does not, and a screenshot cannot tell them apart.
scripts.check:games: npm run check:game && npm run check:merge
scripts._comment_check_timer: The wellness timer engine's arithmetic, asserted without a screen. Pause/resume banking, background catch-up, exactly-once completion, phase boundaries, and the Stretch routine's 300-second total are all claims about numbers, and a screenshot cannot check a number.
scripts._comment_py_checks: Two rule sets here are Python because the engine is Python: services/tools/resume_layout.py (what fits on a résumé page) and services/tools/captions.py (what a subtitle file must look like). Each imports nothing — no PDF library, no Pillow, no token — so its check runs anywhere. py-check.mjs finds the interpreter: python3 on a Mac, python / PYTHON311 on the VM.
scripts._comment_check_multipart: The FLUX.2 image models take multipart form data rather than JSON, and Python's standard library has no encoder for it, so services/tools/multipart.py builds the body by hand. scripts/check-multipart.py parses it back and asserts every part — boundary, headers, binary safety, part order — with no token and no network.
scripts._comment_sounds: Merge's four sounds are synthesized here rather than downloaded, so they are ours outright and the recipe is readable. It refuses to write a file that is silent, which is the bug the first version of this script shipped.
scripts._comment_wellness_sounds: The six wellness screens' cues, bed and spoken phrases — 26 files generated from scripts/lib/wav.mjs and scripts/lib/voice.mjs (a formant voice synthesizer). Seeded noise makes it deterministic, and it refuses a file that is silent, clips, or is long enough to talk over the next phase. See docs/wellness-sound.md.
scripts._comment_icon_preview: make-app-icons.mjs proves the files exist; only a person can say whether the art is any good. This draws every mark three ways — as the store tile, as the adaptive foreground, and at the 60px a home screen gives it — into one contact sheet to be looked at before a store build.
